newsitem.title: FRANCE: French defense minister says satisfied with budget.
newsitem.headline: French defense minister says satisfied with budget.

text.p: French Defense Minister Charles Millon said on Wednesday he was satisfied with a government 1997 draft budget announced earlier, which reflected a 1997-2002 program on military spending.
"I am satisfied with the 1997 budget draft for one simple reason -- it scrupulously respects the law on the military spending program," he told a news conference.

Excluding pensions, the defense budget for 1997 was set at 190.9 billion francs, which at current prices corresponds to the 185 billion francs forecast in constant 1995 prices in the spending program.
The budget for investment was set at 88.70 billion francs after 88.95 billion in 1996.
The budget would also ensure the continuity of France's nuclear deterrent, given a budget of 19.15 billion francs.
This would provide financing for a program to build the new generation nuclear missile launch submarines, called "Le Temeraire" and "Le Vigilant."
